resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance (Resale/CCO inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Township of Rochelle Park Building Department / Code Enforcement (enforcement officer)
resale_co.lead_time: Code says the inspection is done within a reasonable time, not more than 30 days after a complete application. Allow time before closing in case a re-inspection is needed.
requirements: Handrails on inside and outside stairs with more than 3 risers
Vents for all gas appliances in good repair
Hot water heater must have a Township Building Department inspection sticker
GFCI receptacles within 5 feet of kitchen and bathroom sinks
House number visible near the front door, at least 3 1/2 inches high
No oil drippings from oil-fired units; oil tanks not in use must be removed
Sump pump must discharge outside, not into the sanitary sewer
Additions and alterations less than 5 years old must have a valid permit on file; no open permits
No visible safety issues; property maintenance violations corrected
Tax Collector certification that all property taxes are paid (required for all resale certificates)
Sidewalks and curbs inspected with the resale CCO

fees.label: Certificate of compliance, sale of a one family home
fees.quote: For the sale of a one-family homes and individual condominiums, cooperative units and apartment units: $100.

fees.label: Certificate of compliance, sale of a two family home
fees.quote: For the sale of a two-family dwellings: $200.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply to the Building Department (Code Enforcement), 151 West Passaic Street, on the Township form with the fee (check payable to Township of Rochelle Park; payment must accompany the application) and the Tax Collector's paid-taxes certification. Call 201-379-7104 ext. 1000 to schedule. The CCO is not released until all items pass. Apply separately to the Fire Prevention Bureau for the smoke/CO certificate.
resale_co.contact_title: Director of Code Enforcement / Construction Official / Zoning Officer (201-379-7104 ext. 1020, jdimaria@rochelleparknj.gov); Technical Assistant Lisa Ruff

resale_co.notes: Township Code Chapter 75 (Certificates of Compliance, amended in its entirety 12-10-2025 by Ord. No. 1251-25) was read through the ecode360 print view. The 'Home Sale Requirements' file linked from the Building Department page is a scanned 2015 Google Drive PDF; it lists a $100.00 Resale/CCO fee, but the current code sets $100 for one family and $200 for two family sales, so only the code fees are recorded. Quotes from the scanned PDF may not be machine-checkable. Lead paint inspections and landlord registration are rental items, not resale items.

requirements: Smoke alarms meeting NFPA 72 for quantity, type and location, all in working order
Carbon monoxide detector(s) within ten feet of sleeping areas
Secondary power source labeled, if the home has one
No fire extinguisher required since April 2025 (still recommended)
Vacant homes must be scheduled with a property representative present

authorities.name: Rochelle Park Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (Fire Prevention Bureau)
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on calendar/business days between the application and the anticipated closing date. The application is valid for six months; a certificate not used within six months needs a new application.

fees.label: CSACMAC, all other occupancies (1 and 2 family), more than 5 calendar days before closing
fees.quote: All other occupancies Greater than 5 calendar days = $75.00

fees.label: CSACMAC, less than 4 calendar days before closing
Re-inspection
fees.amount: Same as the initial fee paid ($75.00 or $125.00)
fees.quote: Any re-inspection fee(s) issued will be equal to the initial fee paid

authorities.how_to_apply: Complete the Home Resale Fire Inspection (CSACMAC) application and email it with the fee to Lisa Ruff (Lruff@rochelleparknj.gov). After submitting, the applicant must contact the Bureau by email or at 201-587-7750 to schedule; the Bureau no longer calls to schedule. The fee is not refundable.
authorities.contact_title: Bureau Chief (Sredl@rochelleparknj.gov); Secretary Lisa Ruff receives applications

evidence.quote: How Do I File for a Home Re-sale inspection?
Complete & return the linked CSACMAC application, here. The fee schedule is posted below.
Please return all completed applications to Lisa Ruff at Lruff@rochelleparknj.gov
the requirement for a portable fire extinguisher during a CSACMAPFEC inspection is no longer required.
The application is valid for six months.

fire_cert.notes: The fire prevention web page lists fees as 'Greater than 5 calendar days = $75.00' and 'Less than 4 calendar days = $125.00'; the scanned application (revised 5/2026) says '< 4 business days $125'. Neither covers exactly 4 to 5 days, so confirm. The application PDF is scanned, so its quotes may not be machine-checkable. The fire extinguisher is no longer required (Bureau notice citing A3894, as of April 2025).

other_items.label: Paid taxes certification
other_items.detail: A Tax Collector certification that all property taxes are paid is required for all resale certificates.

other_items.label: Sidewalks and curbs
other_items.detail: The Construction Official inspects sidewalks and curbs with applications for certificates of continued occupancy on resale of a residence (Code 161-22G).

other_items.label: Oil tanks
other_items.detail: Oil tanks not in use must be removed for the resale CCO.

other_items.label: Water heater sticker
other_items.detail: The hot water heater must carry a Township Building Department inspection sticker.

open_questions: Is there a current (post-2015) Building Department resale CCO application form and checklist? Only a 2015 scanned file is posted.
Which fire certificate fee applies when the application is 4 to 5 days before closing?
Is there a CCO re-inspection fee? None is published in Chapter 75.
